name: Mboi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2020. Adamawa. In Rainer Vossen & Gerrit J. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 220-230. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Most recent overview of Adamawa groups by the same author; may state group-level tone typology for Ɓəna-Mboi. Paywalled OUP handbook chapter.
Nothing; names, dialects (Gəna, Banga, Handa), Blench 2004/2019 cited.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2019. Bena-Mboi is Benue-Congo. Presentation, Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 24 pp. (= Glottolog ref 580481)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Mboi; 'Mostly Bena-Yungur data, since we have only limited data on the other Bena-Mboi varieties'; a single Mboi form tuŋ 'ear' in a cognate table.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2019. Tonal reconstruction of Bena-Yungur: depressor consonants and directionality of tonal interactions. Presentation, Adamawa Conference, Mainz.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the sister language Bena-Yungur (three-level L M H tone system, TBU = syllable, tone spread and absorption); Mboi is not mentioned; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014 [1992]. Evidence of noun classes in languages of the Yungur (Ɓəna-Mboi) group. Ms. (written version of a 1991 Maiduguri conference paper; German version = Afrika und Übersee 76 (1993): 3-13), Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz, 10 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Mboi (Gulongo) and Haanda nouns are cited with tone marks (e.g. zangáy-ɔ 'louse'); p.1 says explicitly that 'Neither the phonologies nor the tonologies of the languages dealt with are studied in detail', p.2 that tonal differences of suffixes 'mainly remain unheeded'.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014. "ADAMAWA". Slides, JGU Mainz, 4 Feb 2014, 26 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Ɓəna-Mboi appears only as one of five Adamawa noun-class groups.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. Ms. Entry 315 'Mboi cluster'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the entry gives names (Gəna, Banga, Haanda), locations and population figures; its Source(s)/Refs lines are empty.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2011. Ɓəna-Mboi (Yungur) Group. Web page, Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; only that the northern (Livo, Gulongo) and southern (Haanda, Banga) Mboi dialects differ 'mainly phonological[ly]'; cites the Mboi lexeme gə̀nàà 'people' with tone marks.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d./2004. Yungur (Bena-Mboi) group and Mboi wordlists; List of Adamawa languages. Ms., rogerblench.info.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Blench 1990 first separated a 'Gəna' (Mboi) subgroup 'probably on the basis of unpublished data' (Kleinewillinghöfer 2014:1); his site may hold tone-marked Mboi wordlists. The site is captcha-gated to this fetcher (sgcaptcha redirect on every request).

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1993/2014. Ɓəna-Mboi Group (Yungur Group): Basic Wordlist (Swadesh 100). Ms., Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz, 8 pp. (= Glottolog ref 550005, listed as 2015, listed by Glottolog as a wordlist)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; comparative wordlist with columns MBg (Mboi of Gulungo), MB (Mboi of Livo), HA (Mboi of Haanda); forms carry partial tone marks, no prose on prosody.

Nothing; most extensive description (Glottolog's most extensive description) = Meek 1931, 'a wordlist or less'; dialects Banga (bang1349), Gəna (nucl1373), Handa (hand1239); classification refs Bennett 1983, Boyd & Pasch 1988, Kleinewillinghöfer 1996, 2020, Idiatov & Van de Velde 2019.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1996. Die nordwestlichen Adamawa-Sprachen – Eine Übersicht. In Uwe Seibert (ed.), Afrikanische Sprachen zwischen Gestern und Morgen (Frankfurter Afrikanistische Blätter 8), 80-103. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only published typological overview of the Ɓəna-Mboi group by the one linguist who collected Mboi data (1990-95); likely to contain a remark on tone/prosody for the group. Not digitized.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1993. Nominalklassen im Mboi und Ɓəna Lala der Yungur- bzw. Ɓəna-Mboi-Gruppe. Afrika und Übersee 76: 3-13.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The published version of the manuscript read here; would only be needed to cite a printed page instead of the Mainz manuscript. Its English manuscript version contains no stress statement, so low priority.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. 2 (chapter on the Mboi, with wordlist and phrases). London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description of Mboi and the only pre-1990 language material; Meek's vocabularies sometimes carry accent/tone marks and prefatory remarks on pronunciation. Both volumes are on archive.org (tribalstudiesinn0001ckme, tribalstudiesinn0002meek) as controlled-lending items only; scanned text refused (not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Fakuade, Gbenga, Matudi Gambo & Abdullahi Bashir. 2003. Language shift from mother tongues towards Fulfulde in Adamawa State, Nigeria: causes and consequences. Anthropological Linguistics 45(3): 296-315.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; not a phonological description.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, 2 vols. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner. (Glottolog ref 37690; Glottolog's most extensive description for Mboi)
sources.note: Unknown. archive.org holds both volumes (tribalstudiesinn0001ckme, tribalstudiesinn0002meek) as access-restricted lending items; the scanned text could not be reached by automated download; HathiTrust and Google Books API refused the query. Kleinewillinghöfer (2014:1) says it contains 'wordlists and phrases.. on Yungur, Libo, Roba, and Mboi'.
